title: Fuel-ring slow-diffusion negative holds on new seeds 12 and 13 on average: ring-free Df=0.3 twin 10 and 14 persistent splits vs the ringed world's 16 and 10, so 41 vs 39 over three seeds with c20's seed 11
summary: Re-ran c15's nematic-fuelcell world and c20's lowered-D twin (chi_s=0, Df 2.0 -> 0.3, all else equal) on new seeds 12 and 13 (128^2, T=1000), plus chi_s=0 on seed 12. Seed 13: world 10 persistent splits, generation 3, 18 final bodies, 100% ringed, core fuel 0.64; slow-D twin 14, generation 4, 26 final bodies, 0% ringed, core fuel 0.68. Seed 12: world 16 splits, generation 3 (from my review of the claim); slow-D twin 10, generation 3, core fuel 0.77; chi_s=0 10, generation 2, core fuel 0.35. So the twin beats the ring on seed 13 and loses on seed 12, where the twin's rods stay longer at t=1000 despite more core fuel. With c20's seed 11 (15 vs 15) the totals are 41 for the world and 39 for the twin. Per-seed differences of +-4-6 splits go both ways. Uniformly slower fuel diffusion reproduces the ring's effect on division within seed noise.

observations.finding: slowD03/seed13 (14 splits, gen 4) >= world/seed13 (10, gen 3); slowD03/seed12 (10, gen 3) < world seed 12 (16, gen 3; 20261025T1500-c17-review-fuelcell rerun/seed12); totals over seeds 11-13: world 41, twin 39

seeds_run.result: pass: twin matches or exceeds the world (14 vs 10 splits)
partial: twin 10 vs world 16 splits (same as chi_s=0), though core fuel is higher than the world's

verdicts.limitation: Division counts vary by +-40% between arms in both directions from seed to seed, so 3 seeds can show only that the ring and a slow-D twin are not distinguishable, not that they are equal. On seed 12 the twin's rods stay longer, with 0.77 core fuel against the world's 0.56: core fuel alone does not set division. Df=0.3 is not a fitted match (c20's choice). Motility and ring-specific effects other than division were not compared.
